summary.assessment: The run never returns values for a figure without data (5 of 5 true negatives, each with a 'not a data chart' reason) and reads printed numbers without one error (B1, B3, C5 and the CI labels of A3: 48 of 48), with legend, category and panel names verbatim. Bar heights and point estimates read from mark positions are within about 1 % of the axis range (A3, B4, C1, C4), and no figure is wrong, missed or hallucinated. Its recurring weakness is the secondary statistics of a mark: a box median taken at the wrong box edge when no median line is visible (B5, one value 10 % of the range off), a CI widened by 2.8 % (B4), a whisker put at the quartile (C4). Its most damaging single failure is different and silent: in the 264-segment stacked chart C3 one segment boundary is shifted 6-10 points in 12 of 44 bars while every bar still sums to 100 and nothing is declared. The two automatic zeros are not reading errors: B2 traces the line within 0.7 % but leaves the series unnamed, drops 2 of 30 vertices per panel (shifting the later points) and omits the raw dots, and C4 has correct numbers under mislocated panel boxes; axis ranges and panel boxes are the weak part of the record, not the values. It can be trusted on printed-value charts, simple bars, forest plots and pies; dense stacked bars, box-plot medians and the point count of long unlabelled lines need a check.
